findings.description: This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances and is associated with a route table whose default route targets an Internet Gateway. Workloads launched here can become Internet-addressable unless separately constrained.

This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances and is associated with a route table whose default route targets an Internet Gateway. The portal instance is placed in this subnet, making it publicly addressable subject to its security group rules.
The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true. Data stored on this volume may be unencrypted at rest, absent an account-level default encryption setting not shown in this configuration.

The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. The credentials are exposed in source/state and deployed to the publicly reachable instance, enabling unauthorized AWS API access if disclosed.
TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. This security group is attached to an instance in a public subnet with Internet routing, exposing SSH to arbitrary Internet hosts.

All protocols and ports are permitted to 0.0.0.0/0 for egress. This permits arbitrary outbound connections from the publicly reachable instance, including potential command-and-control or data exfiltration following compromise.
The S3 bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. The archived network telemetry may therefore be stored without an explicitly enforced encryption control.
This snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption, so the snapshot can preserve unencrypted data at rest.
